1.note: Four unrelated nouns (durability / wealth / settlement / carpentry) with no lexical overlap, no number or part-of-speech mismatch, and no option a humanities or science passage could not plausibly contain; 'carpentry' is the most concrete but a craft-history passage would use it freely.

2.note: Three methodological/organizational adjectives plus one affective one ('sentimental') is a register split, but 'sentimental' is ordinary humanities vocabulary rather than an off-register technicalism, so nothing can be cut without the stem.

3.note: This is a translation set, and 'faithful' and 'literal' are near-interchangeable in that discourse, so neither can be the unique key; the live axis is 'literal' vs its antonym 'idiomatic', which is exactly what the surviving pair (exacting / idiomatic) reflects.

4.note: equivocal / idiosyncratic / derivative / inconsequential are four distinct evaluative faults on four different axes (clarity, uniqueness, originality, importance) with no pair collapsing and no register outlier.

5.note: 'compounds' is the only plural among three singular/mass nouns and the only option readable as a finite verb, so it cannot fill the same slot as mutation / advantage / time.

6.note: Four third-person-singular transitive verbs, all taking the same kind of abstract object; 'withstands' and 'invites' sit loosely on a resist/attract axis but are not synonyms and neither is excluded.

7.note: 'coeval' and 'successive' form a same-time/one-after-another temporal axis, but that pairing only suggests where the key might live - it excludes nothing, and 'conjectural' and 'unremarkable' remain legal fills.

8.note: generous / provisional / incontrovertible / representative all modify evidence or a sample; 'provisional' vs 'incontrovertible' is an antonym axis but no two options collapse and none is off-register.

9.note: 'dispositive' is courtroom vocabulary - a settled-by-this-alone finding - and sits outside the register of an SAT humanities or science passage, whose other three options (contested / ubiquitous / premonitory) are general academic.

10.note: person / lineage / recipe / trade are all plausible vehicles for transmitted knowledge; 'person' is the most ordinary word but SAT words-in-context keys are routinely ordinary words, so commonness is not a cut.

11.note: exposed / obeyed / resented / corrected are four distinct past participles forming two loose pairs (reveal-vs-fix an error, comply-vs-chafe at a rule) with no lexical synonymy and no grammatical mismatch.

12.note: unusual / unmeasured / imaginary / irrelevant each negate a different property (frequency, quantification, existence, bearing); nothing collapses and no register outlier.

13.note: circular / incomplete / unwarranted / premature are four separable argument faults (assumes its conclusion, has gaps, is unsupported, is drawn too early); 'unwarranted' and 'premature' feel close in the abstract but a passage distinguishes them cleanly, so this is functional overlap, not lexical synonymy.

14.note: Two crossing axes (decisive/secondary for weight, plausible/fanciful for credibility) leave all four options legal; an antonym pairing on its own excludes nothing.

15.note: 'malformed' is the vocabulary of malformed input or a malformed query; academic prose calls a bad question ill-posed or poorly framed, and the other three (academic / contested / unanswerable) are all natural modifiers of 'question'.

16.note: reversible / predictable / accidental / gradual each name a different property of a process (direction, lawfulness, intent, rate) with no pair collapsing.

17.note: 'evaporation' and 'drainage' both remove water from a site and so overlap functionally, but they are mechanistically distinct (to air vs into the ground) and a passage separates them easily; 'settlement' is the odd process but is not excluded.

18.note: 'surpassed' and 'outgrown' both mean superseded when said of a theory or method, so neither can be the unique key; 'forgotten' and 'abandoned' survive because passive loss and deliberate relinquishment are genuinely distinct.

19.note: 'frugality' and 'spareness' are the same austerity/plainness notion in noun form and cancel each other; 'prosperity' is their antonym and 'machinery' is the concrete outlier, both of which survive.

20.note: 'publicize' belongs to publicity and marketing rather than to the scholarly register of discern / chronicle / instruct, which are the three verbs such a passage would use of an observer or a record.

21.note: preserved / translated / invented all take a text, tradition or artifact as object, while 'disciplined' selects a person or a practice, so it cannot fill the same slot as the other three.
